In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the best protection scheme for the transmission line is the one which minimizes the probability of occurrence of voltage sags in a way that the probability of occurrence is lower than the customer voltage tolerance.

the impact of protection scheme on the quality of supply depends on a number of factors, namely, the type of protection scheme, the short circuit power, the site voltage exposure and the equipment tolerance curve.
the use of the probabilistic methodology allows utilities to support capital investment decisions in new protection schemes design, aiming at improving the voltage quality as regards voltage sages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact on voltage quality of the protection schemes used for transmission lines is not straightforward and should be carefully evaluated.
probabilistic assessment is the best approach to evaluate the performance of a protection scheme, as it takes into account the uncertainties of the problem.
, for voltage sag assessment, the probabilistic approach is a more realistic approach to be used in the power system analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of the transmission line protection scheme on the voltage sag performance indices is not straightforward.
the impact of protection schemes on voltage sags depends not only on the fault clearing time but also on other factors like the fault location and the short circuit power.
, for a given site, the best primary protection scheme is not necessarily the one with the lowest fault clearance time.
